title: R4306: Dutch diplomatic cipher, transcribed with CTTS and solved with Opus 5.5

documents.shelfmark: Riksarkivet, Stockholm, Chifferklaver låda II:133; DECODE R4306
documents.date: Undated; pencilled 1632?; references letters of 23 February and 13 March
documents.route: Unknown sender → "Mr ?ilick (Wilick?)", Amsterdam (address leaf, DECODE image I25833, read 18 Oct 2026)

plaintext.source: No interlinear or marginal decipherment on the supplied cipher page. No historical plaintext or matched archive key used in the contributed solution.

transcription.source: George Lasry’s CTTS project; Codex merged separated digit boxes; current post-review transcription supplied with the Opus 5.5 solution.
transcription.notes: 35 CTTS rows, 463 selections; two date-numeral selections (285=23, d13=13) excluded from cipher counts. Position-label histogram matches transcription exactly. DECODE lists three record pages; only this one cipher page is submitted.

system.summary: An alphabetical numerical substitution, 30–52, with nulls and four unresolved three-digit nomenclator codes.

diacritics.note: Dots/colons separate numbers; superscript marks on date numerals do not select a cipher alphabet.

system.doubled_letters: Encoded twice; no general doubling operator established.
system.sibling_key: No archive or sibling key used. Earlier survey tested R4296 and R4310 unsuccessfully.
system.notes: 23 alphabet positions (30–52), 21 observed; 45=q and 51=x are predictions. Source header calls this 24 letters but lists only 23. Fifteen observed null classes (34 occurrences), plus unobserved null 13 in the source key. No j, v or z assignment. Date labels 285 and d13 represent literal 23 and 13; they are not nomenclator entries.

prior_solution.where: The 21 September repository survey reports failed attempts; DECODE is still Non-decrypted on 17 October 2026. No prior plaintext was located in the limited exact-phrase search; no priority claim.

conditions.human_role: George Lasry directed the work, supplied the CTTS material, and supplied the edited Dutch reading, English translation and contextual notes. He confirms: transcribed with CTTS, then solved with Opus 5.5. Codex packaged the PR and checked counts, glyphs and five mechanical lines.

solution.what: Project attempt (former entry riksarkivet4306): fetched the 14 DECODE records of catalogue 207 with the project cookie; R4306 (Chifferklaver låda II:133, reported as addressed to "Mr ?ilick" at Amsterdam, pencilled "1632?") is one of four unrelated groups.
Project attempt: agent transcription of R4306 from the DECODE images (463 numbers; re-measured 14 Oct 2026 as 492 tokens, 51 distinct), now targets/sweden4306/project_attempt/r4306_transcription.txt.
Project attempt: IoC 0.078 (monoalphabetic); '34 42' x31.

Project attempt: simple-substitution and homophonic annealing over quadgram models in nl, de, la, fr, sv, en, it, es, pt, da (targets/riksarkivet1628/solve_num.py, qg.py), also with low/high numbers as word breaks; best about -4.3/char against about -2.5 for real text, after a search bug and a backoff-model artefact were fixed.
Project attempt: re-transcribed keeping the scribe's digit variants (34/74, 40/4o/9o, 30/3o/70/7o; 465 tokens, 62 distinct; project_attempt/r4306_v2.txt) and annealed again: no fit.
Project attempt: fetched 70 Chifferklaver låda II key records (R4259-R4329); tested the Siebenbürgen key R4310 and the 1632 word-end-30 key R4296: no fit. The other 68 were not tried.
Earlier riksarkivet1628 survey reports failed numerical attacks in multiple languages and rejected keys R4296/R4310. These are prior attempts, not new runs in this contribution.
Project attempt split from the catalogue-207 group entry riksarkivet1628 as its own entry riksarkivet4306 under the one-key rule; both transcriptions re-measured. No new attack.
CTTS digit selections were merged into numerical units; current supplied snapshot contains 463 selections in 35 rows. Subsequent sign corrections are recorded in the preserved source-key comments.

George Lasry confirms that Opus 5.5 solved the cipher after CTTS transcription. The working-key header describes crib dragging; the result is an alphabetical number mapping with nulls. No historical plaintext or external key supplied the recovery. Exact prompts and run settings are not reconstructed.

Matched all 463 position labels to transcription counts; counted 461 cipher elements after excluding date numerals, and reapplied the current key to exactly five manuscript lines without correcting their spelling.

Checked public DECODE metadata: Riksarkivet Chifferklaver låda II:133, three record pages, broad 1600–1699 catalogue range, blank correspondents/languages and Non-decrypted status. Image manager requires login; only the supplied cipher page is independently inspected here.

Deduplicated under one key, one entry: the project's attempted-open entry riksarkivet4306 (same record R4306) folded into this contributed entry; its transcriptions moved to project_attempt/, its page made a stub pointing to sweden4306.html, its ledger rows removed. The contributed key, reading and counts were not changed.

Opened R4306's two other DECODE views at full resolution: address leaf I25833 ('Aen Mr. ?ilick (Wilick?) ... Amsterdam', confirming the earlier survey's Amsterdam) and wrapper I25834 (II:104, '1600- Chifferbref till ... i Amsterdam'). The address leaf carries a 3-line cipher note in its right margin with codes 113 and 101.
Applied the contributed key to the address-leaf note: 'ler.,[torn]hlden / [113]naeldan / kn[101]na..mk'; all Caesar offsets of a 24-letter alphabet and the R4287 sequential key also tried: no Dutch.

A faint list on the wrapper image (Nz ..., Oz ..., Tz Rex Polon., Vz Victoria ...) matched to the last leaf of R4305 (Brandenstein 1630 key, II:132, filed next to R4306): a show-through/offset from that key, not R4306's nomenclator.

Surveyed every Chifferklaver låda II key record on DECODE for an alphabet a=30 ... y=52 with a 100+ nomenclator: the archivists' wrapper labels ('a = 7, 35, 51' etc.) of 43 records, the pages of the unlabelled and wrapperless records, and the never-downloaded R4319-R4321. None matches. R4287 ('diverse chiffernycklar ... av okänd proveniens') is a similar sequential type with another alphabet (a=2/28/10, c=31).

R4319 (Jacob du Moulin, 1650) is the same chancery template at another offset: sequential alphabet a=20 ... z=43, then an alphabetical nomenclator from 101 (101 Archangel ... 112 Ambassadeur, 113 Amsterdam; B from 120). By analogy R4306's 101-114 would be A/B-initial words. Not testable on five occurrences; offered to George as a proposal.

Checked the doubtful spots (lines 4-5 ekll|men, line 33 Mar..y) on the page image: the scribe's tailed 0 makes 30/38 and 40/43 ambiguous; no better reading can be forced. Gap reclassified as illegible.

Brett Burford (issue #47): independent keyless re-reading (own transcription, annealing with a 17th-c. Dutch model, nothing seeded) agrees with Lasry's key on all 21 values, 447/463 groups (96.5%) and 411/422 letters (97.4%); flags L12 g7, L20 g9, L23 g13 (4/9 form rather than 8), L26 g4, L34 g1. Reading the scribe's tailed o as 8 turns the address-leaf note (I25833) into Dutch: ter... / ...niet dan... / in [101] na... (42 38 34 48 33 30 = n i e t d a). Recorded as a proposal; the image could not be re-checked here on 21 Oct (DECODE cookie expired).

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): George Lasry's CTTS transcription and token file, edited Dutch reading, translation and key (key.txt), the five-line mechanical excerpt, this project's earlier transcriptions, and, as a separate file, the address-leaf note with Burford's proposed reading copied from NOTES to texts/address_note.md.

validation.notes: The requested five manuscript lines contain only 62 literal letters, below the validator minimum of 80; no full mechanical decryption is included. No statistical accuracy claim is made.

outcome.method_basis: Transcribed with CTTS, then solved with Opus 5.5, as confirmed by George Lasry; no historical plaintext or external key used.
outcome.fraction_read_source: counts.json: 422 assigned letter occurrences / 427 non-null cipher occurrences. Five unresolved code occurrences; 34 nulls and two date-numeral selections excluded. Assignment coverage, not verified meaningful-reading accuracy.

credits.note: Directed the work and supplied the CTTS project, edited Dutch text, translation and context. Transcribed with CTTS, then solved with Opus 5.5.
issue #47: independent keyless re-reading agreeing with Lasry's key; address-leaf note read as Dutch with the tailed o = 8

gaps.item: Codes 105, 106, 113 and 114 (and 101 in the address-leaf note)
gaps.detail: No key with this alphabet (a=30 ... y=52) is among the 61 Chifferklaver låda II key records on DECODE (the wrappers' 'a =' labels and the unlabelled keys checked 18 Oct 2026, R4319-R4321 newly fetched); R4306's own three views carry no gloss; five occurrences of four values are too few to rebuild the nomenclator. The sister template R4319 (Jacob du Moulin 1650: sequential alphabet, then an alphabetical nomenclator from 101) suggests A/B-initial words, a structural proposal only.

Checked on the page image 18 Oct 2026: the scribe writes 0 as a tailed o, so 30/38 and 40/43 are ambiguous (mondeling(e) ... ekll|men; Mar..y written 41:30:46:3ø:52); the rest are the scribe's own slips, and no better image or contemporary decipherment exists. George's editorial restorations stand.

gaps.item: Cipher note on the address leaf (image I25833, 3 lines, about 22 numbers, partly torn away)
gaps.detail: Burford (issue #47) reads it as Dutch when the tailed o is taken as 8 (40->48, 30->38): ter... / ...niet dan... / in [101] na...; a hole loses 2-3 groups. Needs a check of each digit on image I25833.

The letter names neither; the wrapper (II:104, '1600- Chifferbref till ... i Amsterdam') and the pencilled 1632? are archivists' estimates. Recipient address read on I25833: 'Aen Mr. ?ilick (Wilick?) ... Amsterdam', first letter of the surname unclear. Only Riksarkivet provenance records could date it.

outcome.notes: Belongs to: Riksarkivet key-box and Oxenstierna ciphers. Exactly five mechanical lines included; the full Dutch reading and translation are supplied editions. No full mechanical decryption or established year/identity claimed. Escalation 18 Oct 2026 (Claude, for George Lasry's review): box keys, R4306's other views and the address-leaf note worked; no gap remains workable from DECODE.

texts.label: R4306, Riksarkivet Chifferklaver låda II:133, a Dutch cipher letter to Amsterdam, [1632?] (George Lasry)
texts.summary: A Dutch letter addressed 'Aen Mr. ?ilick ... Amsterdam', pencilled 1632?: the writer will answer orally, reports jealousy beginning between the [106] and the [114] [105] envoys, knows [113]'s whole intention and has kept a close watch on him, and has received the recipient's letters of 23 February and 13 March. Reading and translation are George Lasry's (transcribed with CTTS, solved with Opus 5.5); the project_attempt/ files are this project's earlier transcriptions, and texts/address_note.md the cipher note on the address leaf, with Brett Burford's proposed reading, which his reading does not cover.
